description.content: This value does not change for the life of the tabset, so it is safe to use as an effect dependency. Use useParentTabsetState for values that should trigger a re-render.

fields.name: addTab
fields.type: (tab: TabNode<TabData>, options?: {index?: number | undefined; select?: boolean | undefined}) => boolean

description.content: Close the tabset, along with any tabs it contains (see WorkspaceImperativeHandle.closeTabset).
Collapse the tabset to just its header (see WorkspaceImperativeHandle.collapseTabset).
Expand the tabset if it is collapsed (see WorkspaceImperativeHandle.expandTabset).
Move the tabset out of the layout, to float above it (see WorkspaceImperativeHandle.floatTabset).
The tabset is currently collapsed (in the model).

A tabset may be shown collapsed (or expanded) unlike the model: while a separator is being dragged (before the model changes), and when it's collapsed to fit (see TabsetNode.collapsible); useParentTabsetState().isCollapsed reflects how it's shown.
The tabset currently floats above the layout (see WorkspaceModel.floating).
This has no effect on the only tabset in a workspace (see ParentTabsetState.isRoot).
Restore the tabset if it is maximized.
Select a tab within this tabset (e.g. from an overflow menu; see useTabListOverflow).
This has no effect if the tab isn't in this tabset; use WorkspaceImperativeHandle.selectTab to select a tab in any tabset.
Id of the Workspace that contains the tabset.
